relationships.subject: CGRP
relationships.evidence_quote: Indeed, combined RNAscope ISH and immunofluorescence analysis confirmed that in CGRP-treated animals, both the Ucn1 mRNA (Student t test, P = 0.0004) expression (Fig. 7C) and UCN1 peptide immunosignal (Student's t test, P = 0.0007; Fig. 7D) was significantly higher than in controls.

relationships.subject: CGRP
relationships.evidence_quote: In the DRN, CGRP treatment decreased both the 5-HT (Student t test, P = 0.03; Fig. 8A) and TPH2 (Student t test, P = 0.01; Fig. 8B) content of the serotonergic neurons.

relationships.subject: CGRP
relationships.evidence_quote: Calcitonin gene–related peptide treatment significantly reduced the periorbital withdrawal threshold compared with saline (Student t test, P = 8.25 × 10−13; Fig. 6B).

relationships.subject: EWcp/UCN1 neurons
relationships.evidence_quote: Interestingly, after the ablation of EWcp/UCN1 neurons, the saline treatment significantly reduced periorbital withdrawal threshold compared with nonablated controls, (P = 0.0001), and CGRP treatment did not change it further (Fig. 9B).

relationships.subject: EWcp/UCN1 neurons
relationships.evidence_quote: Green fluorescent protein and UCN1 double-positive fibers were observed in the STN in samples of mice subjected to AAV8-GFP injection into the EWcp (Fig. 5C).

key_findings: Peripheral CGRP activates urocortinergic EWcp neurons, raising Ucn1 mRNA and peptide, and lowers TPH2 and 5-HT in the dorsal raphe.
EWcp/UCN1 neurons project directly to the spinal trigeminal nucleus, and ablating them induces hyperalgesia.
